Reference / fs/root

fs/root#

Reads below one directory that cannot be led out of it: entries are reached by names, one at a time, and links are never followed.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

let root = FileRoot(directory: Directory(path: Path("public")));
defer root.close();
let page = root.entry(["docs", "index.html"]);
defer page.close();
let head = page.bytes_at(0, 4096);
let names = root.entry(["docs"]).names(100);

Description#

Reads below one directory that cannot be led out of it: entries are reached by names, one at a time, and links are never followed.

Each name must be a plain name, without / or .., so a request for ../secret is refused rather than resolved. An entry must be a regular file or a directory. Entries keep their own descriptors and stay usable after the root is closed. http/static serves files this way.

Public API#

object FileRoot#

object FileRoot does Closing

Eager explicit root acquisition. Children own independent descriptors and remain valid after root close; coordinates never become joined ambient paths.

Opens directory now; FileError when it cannot.

RootedEntry.bytes_at#

At most limit bytes (1 to 1048576) from offset of a regular file; [] past its end.

RootedEntry.piece#

async piece(offset is int, limit is int) is @byte

The bytes from offset on, at most limit of them, read off the program's thread (#121): a slow disk holds up only the task that awaits it. Past the end of the file the piece is empty.
